title.narrative: NIHR DA 1: Development of a research partnership for improving monitoring and treatment of neonatal infections in Bangladesh

description.narrative:
A low- and middle-income country (LMIC) led award led by the Child Health Research Foundation in Bangladesh which aims to establish a research partnership with the UK-based Centre for Antimicrobial Optimisation Network (CAMO-Net).
Neonatal deaths remain a major challenge to Bangladesh in its pursuit of achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by 2030. Specifically, infections are a significant cause of neonatal deaths in Bangladesh, and the rise of antimicrobial-resistant infections continues to exacerbate this issue and threaten progress made. Commencing in January 2025 this partnership, known as the Bangladesh Initiative for Advancing Research on Neonatal Infections (BARN), aims to build clinical research capacity in Bangladesh to better monitor and manage neonatal infections. The BARN initiative will lay the foundation for the transfer of knowledge and skills related to cutting-edge biomonitoring and surveillance technologies from the Global North to the Global South, enabling their critical evaluation and use in LMIC settings. This will be done through the co-development of two pilot studies aimed at examining the use of continuing monitoring systems for non-invasive tracking of antibiotics and biomarkers in neonates to optimise antimicrobial usage, as well as to use molecular epidemiological methods to track and reduce healthcare-associated infections in neonates.

The award has five objectives:
1. To strengthen the ongoing partnership between the Child Health Research Foundation in Bangladesh and UK-based Centre for Antimicrobial Optimisation Network (CAMO-Net) through stakeholder engagement meetings. 2. To examine the use of continuous monitoring systems for non-invasive tracking of antibiotics and biomarkers in neonates to optimise antimicrobial usage. 3. To use molecular epidemiological methods to track and reduce healthcare-associated infections in neonates. 4. To conduct retrospective analysis of clinical and epidemiological data on neonatal infections available from four hospitals in Bangladesh. 5. To develop training workshops for early career researchers in Bangladesh, focusing on research methods, ethics, and project management.
